correctness.rationale: For each scaled party the Eq. (18) map has nonnegative coefficients summing to one. Tensor distributivity therefore expresses every multi-parameter output as a convex combination of subset partial transposes. Trace-norm convexity bounds every interior value by the largest vertex value, and each vertex realizes exactly one subset partial transpose. Positivity follows from convexity of the positive cone. Complementary subsets have equal trace norm because they differ by full transposition. These steps prove the stated equality for every finite-dimensional state without numerical extrapolation.

value.rationale: The result converts a continuous multi-parameter criterion and source-defined trace-norm optimization into a finite list of ordinary PPT/negativity checks for every state and finite local dimension. It proves that the source's endpoint behavior is universal, eliminates numerical parameter scans for this map family, and clarifies that generic interior scaling points carry no independent detection strength. This is a structural simplification of the proposed multipartite method rather than a routine recomputation of one example.
